answer: Collateral-bounded influence resists sybils: an identity's earning and voting weight is capped by the live stake it keeps locked, not by its mere existence. A raven-flock of empty fakes carries hollow weight — zero stake, zero influence — so headcount alone buys nothing. To wield N units of influence an attacker must lock N units of the same umber-dark collateral an honest single agent posts for its one share. Splitting capital across many heads only divides one influence budget, never multiplies it, and a caught identity's stake is slashed so the cap stays enforced.
